content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 85+ values), often overshooting by 2–5%.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: tends to forecast prices back toward historical averages, missing recent volatility or trend continuation.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements, particularly in the 10–20 day window — model reacts slower to new data.
- Model underestimates downward trends in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true prices show a sharp decline.
- Model overconfident in short-term volatility — forecasts show wider swings than actual price behavior, especially in the last 5 days.
- Model fails to capture “rebound” patterns after sharp drops — often underestimates recovery or overestimates continuation of decline.
